title: Senior's toolkit: classes, types and type checkers
summary: Dataclass options, Protocols, a useful __repr__, and running mypy and pyright the way teams do.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: classes, types and type checkers
steps.body: Python teams in 2026 write small dataclasses, describe what they need with Protocols, and run a type checker in CI. These are the options and commands that matter.

toolkit.what: Generate `__init__`, `__repr__` and `__eq__`. `frozen` makes instances read-only (and hashable); `slots` saves memory and stops typos creating new attributes.
flags: no `__dict__`; a misspelt attribute is an error (3.10+)
all fields must be passed by name (3.10+)

toolkit.what: A fresh mutable default for each instance. `tags: list = []` is refused with a ValueError for exactly this reason.
flags: a new empty list per object
keep a secret or huge field out of the repr

toolkit.what: Copy a (frozen) dataclass with some fields changed: the way to "modify" an immutable value.
flags: a new object, the old one unchanged
a plain dict, for JSON or logging

toolkit.what: Describe the methods you need, not a base class. Any object with those methods fits (structural typing), which keeps tests and fakes simple.
flags: the shape a parameter must have
toolkit.example:
class Notifier(Protocol):
    def send(self, to: str, text: str) -> None: ...

toolkit.what: Check type hints without running the code. `--strict` turns on all optional checks, including untyped functions.
flags: every optional check on; the usual setting for new code
silence errors for libraries without type information
silence one line, for one error code only

toolkit.what: Microsoft's type checker; the same engine powers Pylance in VS Code, so CI and the editor agree.
Ask the checker what type it inferred at that spot. mypy and pyright print it; at run time (3.11+, from typing) it prints the runtime type.
What logs, the debugger and the REPL show. Make it unambiguous; `!r` puts quotes round strings.
flags: repr of each field, so `'5'` and `5` look different

code: from dataclasses import dataclass, replace, FrozenInstanceError
steps.explain: The generated `__repr__` shows each field with `repr()`. Frozen instances refuse assignment, `replace` builds a new object, and the generated `__eq__` compares fields.

steps.prompt: Match each dataclass option to its effect.
pairs: assigning a field raises an error
a misspelt attribute cannot be created
instances can be sorted by their fields
every field must be passed by name
each instance gets its own new list

steps.prompt: CI's type check fails with this. What is the right fix?
code: src/billing.py:14: error: Item "None" of "User | None" has no attribute "email"  [union-attr]
options: `find_user` can return None: handle it (`if user is None: raise UserNotFound(id)`) before using `user.email`
Add `# type: ignore` to the line
Change the return type of `find_user` to `User` without changing its code
steps.explain: The checker found a real crash path: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'email'`. After the `if user is None` check, the checker narrows `user` to `User`. Ignoring it only hides the bug.

steps.prompt: Importing a module fails with `ValueError: mutable default <class 'list'> for field items is not allowed: use default_factory`. The class has `items: list[str] = []`. Why does dataclass refuse it?
options: Every instance would share the same list, so adding to one cart would add to all; use `field(default_factory=list)`
Dataclasses cannot have list fields at all
The type hint must be `List` from typing, not `list`
Defaults must come before fields without defaults
steps.explain: A default is evaluated once, when the class is defined. This is the same trap as `def f(items=[])`, and dataclasses stop it for lists, dicts and sets.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Reach for `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` for any value object, and a `Protocol` when a function needs "something that can send". Run mypy or pyright in CI and in your editor, and treat each error as a possible crash to understand, not a line to silence.
